prompt: Editorial on-model wedding photograph at night, vertical 9:16 frame, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels. The camera is behind the ear: photographed from behind her, about 35 degrees to the right of straight behind and level with the ear, looking at the back of her right ear. Her head is turned fully away from the camera, so the whole face is hidden behind the back of her head and jaw: no eyelash, eyelid, brow, cheek, nose or lip breaks the outline of the head anywhere in the frame. To the right of the ear there is only the side of the neck, the back edge of the jaw and loose hair, and the right edge of the frame cuts across the jaw about 3 cm in front of the ear, so the outline of the cheek and face never enters the frame; no eye, eyelash, eyebrow, temple or nose shows anywhere, not even as a silhouette against the lights. (In an earlier attempt the head was only partly turned away and an eyelash and the tail of an eyebrow showed past the cheek at the right edge; that must never happen.) Her hair is drawn back into a glossy dark bun high on the back of the crown, wrapped in a white mogra gajra; the bun sits in the top half of the frame, at the upper left, and below the earlobe there is only the bare nape, neck and blouse. One earring is worn tip-down on the right earlobe of an Indian woman in her late thirties with warm wheatish skin, natural texture and fine downy hair at the nape; an oxblood raw-silk blouse at the shoulder. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Copy the left stud in reference 1, which faces the camera straight on, and ignore its plaster block. Reference 2 shows the same stud worn at its true 15 mm size on an earlobe: use it only for how big the star is against the lobe, and take nothing else from it: not the person, not her face, lips, nose or jaw, not the front view, not her clothes, hair or background. The piece: a stud, one of an identical pair, a 15 mm four-pointed star with concave sides, worn tip-down: 1 row of about 44 tiny round pave stones traces the outline; inside, 4 clear pear-cut stones, each in a polished frame with 1 bead prong at its point, aim out at the 4 tips; centre: 1 round clear stone in a bezel on a small 4-pointed plate; 8 slim open gaps flank the pears; post and butterfly back; 18k gold tone, high polish. Copy the left stud in reference 1 exactly. The outline is ONE row of about 11 round stones along each concave side, each stone as wide as the 18k gold tone border is thick, with tiny 18k gold tone prongs between them: never a band of micro pave 2 stones wide. There is no pave between the pears and no second row around any pear. Each pear is one large faceted clear stone with large clean facets, like the pears in reference 1, not a cluster of small stones and not a crushed-ice speckle, in its own thin smooth polished frame; its pointed end faces its tip of the star, its rounded end faces the centre, and one round bead prong sits at its point. Between each pear and the outline, and between neighbouring pears, 8 slim open windows show the skin through the piece. The centre is 1 round clear stone (round, not oval) in a smooth round bezel on a small flat 4-pointed plate whose 4 points reach out between the pears. Every prong, frame, bezel, plate and the outline are the same 18k gold tone. (In earlier attempts pave dividers filled the 8 windows, the pears became glittery clusters, the centre became an upright oval with no 4-pointed plate, and the outline became a double band of tiny stones; all of that is wrong.) It must stay a sharp four-pointed star with an open pave outline around 4 outward-pointing pears, never a rounded four-leaf shape or a solid pave face, never more than 4 pears. Do not redesign, restyle or resize it. SCALE, the most important instruction: the star is 15 mm tip to tip, the size of a shirt button. The ear, about 58 mm from the top of the helix to the bottom of the lobe, is about four star-heights tall, so the star is about a quarter of the ear's height. The star is no taller than the earlobe itself: it sits on the lobe, its top tip just below the bottom of the ear bowl (the concha), and its lower tip stops at the lobe's lower edge, which stays visible as a curve of skin below it; it never hangs below the lobe onto the jaw or neck. A true soft contact shadow sits on the skin of the lobe all around the star's edge. The frame is about 13 cm wide at the ear, so the star spans about one ninth of the frame width. (In earlier attempts the star came out a third to two thirds too big, 20 to 24 mm, and hung below the lobe; that is wrong.) WORLD: far behind, out of focus, the underside of a red and saffron striped wedding shamiana strung with hundreds of warm tungsten fairy lights, melting into large, soft, perfectly round bokeh discs, seen beyond the back of the head in the upper left and down the left edge of the frame. LIGHT: one large soft key from the left, cool daylight at about 5000 K, lights the ear and the stud; one small hard specular kicker from above right draws a crisp edge along the 18k gold tone and puts one pure-white catchlight in each pear and the centre stone. The only tungsten is in the background bokeh. The metal must match the pale warm yellow 18k gold tone of reference 1, never copper, rose or orange. (In earlier attempts the tungsten turned the metal coppery orange.) COMPOSITION: the top of the ear is 22 percent of the way down the frame and the earlobe ends at 48 percent; the stud's centre sits 44 percent of the way down and about 70 percent across. The top 35 percent is the dark crown and back of the head, the bun and calm, darker canopy bokeh, for a title on the left. From 55 percent down, everything is calm bare nape, neck and blouse in soft shadow, for a caption band. (In earlier attempts the stud sat 60 percent of the way down because a low bun was kept whole in the frame; come closer and keep the ear high.) The picture stays a clean, modern, pin-sharp wedding photograph: the VHS effects are added later as overlays, so no VHS look, no scan lines, no star-shaped glints, no starburst on the fairy lights (they stay round soft discs), no lens flare, no glow. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no timestamps. No face, no eyes, no eyebrows. Only this one earring; no other jewellery. It must stay a sharp four-pointed star with an open pave outline around 4 outward-pointing pears, never a rounded four-leaf shape or a solid pave face, never more than 4 pears.

Witty editorial still-life advertising photograph, vertical 9:16 frame, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels. Close and low, the camera about 15 degrees above the silk: a plain black VHS video cassette from the 1990s lies flat on pooled oxblood raw silk, its long front edge (the 25 mm tall spine that carries a blank cream paper label strip) facing the lens almost square-on and running across the whole width of the frame; both ends of the cassette are outside the left and right edges of the frame. Above and behind that edge, the cassette's matte black top face recedes as a narrow, foreshortened band with one clear window showing brown tape wound on a white reel hub, soft; its far half and back rim melt into deep blur. The cream label strip is completely blank. On the silk directly in front of the label edge, the pair of earrings stands side by side a finger's width apart, each piece touching the label edge behind it: the left one shows its barrel-shaped brushed front face, the right one is turned to show the C opening and the depth of the band. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. It confirms the brushed grain and the scale; leave out the cardamom pod. The piece: 1 pair of chunky hoops, each a short C of 1 wide, softly domed band: barrel-shaped front face 14 mm tall x 9.8 mm wide, band about 6 mm deep, rounded pillowy edges, smooth inner face, 0 stones, 0 visible hinge, post or ridge; soft brushed satin 18k gold tone with fine straight parallel brush lines, pale warm yellow; both pieces the same 18k gold tone all over. It must stay matte brushed satin, never mirror-polished, never silver tone, never ridged or hammered. Do not redesign, restyle or resize it. SCALE, the most important instruction: each earring is only 14 mm tall and 9.8 mm wide; the cassette is full size, 187 mm long, 103 mm deep and 25 mm thick, so it is huge next to the pair. Standing in front of the cassette's 25 mm front edge, each earring reaches only a little above halfway up it: the label edge towers over the pair. About nineteen of these earrings standing side by side would fit along the cassette's length, and about nine side by side would span the width of the frame. The frame is about 9 cm wide and 16 cm tall at the pair, so each earring's height is about 9 percent of the frame's height, and the pair with its gap spans about 45 percent of the frame width. A dark, true contact shadow sits under each piece where it stands on the silk and where it touches the label edge. (In earlier attempts the earrings stood on top of the cassette, its top was seen from too high, and each earring came out nearly as tall as the cassette is thick, one and a half to two times its real size; that must not happen again: the earrings are small and the cassette is big.) LIGHT: one large soft warm fill from the upper left; one small hard light right beside the lens, like a 1990s on-camera video light, throws a crisp, hard-edged dark shadow of each earring onto the cream label behind it and spreads into one broad soft sheen along each brushed dome, never a hot white spot. The silk in front of the pair, toward the camera, falls into deep, almost black shadow, so nothing warm or red faces the pair: the brushed metal reflects only the dark room, the black plastic and the cream label, and stays the pale warm yellow of reference 1 all over, with no pink, red or copper reflection band and no clipped white patch. (In earlier attempts a copper-pink stripe reflected from the silk crossed the lower part of the left earring.) COMPOSITION: the tops of the earrings sit 40 percent of the way down the frame and their bottoms at 49 percent, never lower than 50 percent; the label edge behind them runs from about 33 to 49 percent. The pair stands slightly right of centre, its middle about 56 percent across, so a long stretch of blank label shows to its left. The top 33 percent is the dark, deeply blurred top of the cassette and dark out-of-focus oxblood silk behind it, calm for a title. From 52 percent down, the silk falls into soft deep shadow, calm for a caption band. Palette: oxblood, cocoa, matte black, cream, warm tungsten; the 18k gold tone is the only warm metal. The photograph is clean, modern and pin-sharp: no VHS look, no scan lines, no star-shaped glints, no lens flare, no glow; effects are added later. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no timestamps. No brand marks on the cassette; the label stays blank. The black plastic is plain: no embossed or moulded letters, numbers, dots, arrows or symbols on its rim, top or edges; the only texture is the fine square knurled grip pattern. (In earlier attempts a row of blurred embossed dots ran along the cassette's back rim.) No people, no face, no eyes, no eyebrows, no hands, no other jewellery, no water. Only this one pair. It must stay matte brushed satin, never mirror-polished, never silver tone, never ridged or hammered.
